guide.title: Relationships and word families
guide.rule: Learn combinations such as a close bond, a striking resemblance and have something in common. The suffix -hood can name a stage or social condition.
guide.example: The cousins have a close relationship.

title: Mental and physical development
test: The body, the mind and development

guide.title: Remember and remind
guide.rule: Remember concerns bringing something back to mind; remind someone means help that person remember. Mind expressions have whole-phrase meanings.
guide.example: The students learned to take turns.

guide.title: Health words as language
guide.rule: Distinguish related forms such as allergy / allergic and breath / breathe. The supplied health recordings are comprehension material, not individual advice.
guide.example: The menu lists the ingredients clearly.

guide.title: Collocations for everyday life
guide.rule: Say make a decision, make a living and set a goal. Optimist, pessimist and realist describe different attitudes, not fixed types you must assign to yourself.
guide.example: The club offers a variety of leisure activities.

guide.title: Research language
guide.rule: Define a study’s scope and distinguish sources, methods and findings. Conduct is a verb in conduct research; funding supports an activity.
guide.example: The researchers defined the scope of the study.

guide.title: Accuracy and fluency
guide.rule: Accuracy concerns correct language; fluency concerns the flow of speech. Practise meaning and word combinations as well as individual words.
guide.example: The teacher explained the expression clearly.

guide.title: Travel senses
guide.rule: A journey is travel between places; a trip often includes a visit and return. Learn accommodation and luggage as normally uncountable nouns in these meanings.
guide.example: The itinerary includes three coastal villages.

guide.title: Time and order
guide.rule: On time means at the planned time; in time means early enough. Chronological ordering and words such as subsequently make a sequence clear.
guide.example: The events are arranged in chronological order.

guide.title: Living things and their parts
guide.rule: Flora refers to plants and fauna to animals. A predator hunts prey; distinguish a natural habitat from a particular den or burrow.
guide.example: The project protects the animals and their habitat.

guide.title: Space word families
guide.rule: Learn atmosphere / atmospheric, gravity / gravitational and Moon / lunar in context. Capitalise Earth when naming our planet.
guide.example: The satellite follows an orbit around Earth.

guide.title: Descriptions and building
guide.rule: Learn material and building combinations such as a traditional brick house. Build means construct a structure; build up can mean develop confidence or a relationship.
guide.example: The cottage has ornate wooden ceilings.

guide.title: A device and its function
guide.rule: Describe what a device does and which feature serves a purpose. Computer memory, digital platforms and tracking progress differ from everyday senses of those words.
guide.example: The portable device stores digital information.

guide.title: Trends and interpretation
guide.rule: Distinguish recorded figures from projections. Current means present-day in current trends; a joint venture is a cooperative business project.
guide.example: The two companies formed a joint venture.

guide.title: Problem-solving combinations
guide.rule: Say address a problem, find a solution to it and reach a compromise. Exacerbate makes a problem worse; remedy improves it.
guide.example: The council needs to address the housing problem.

guide.title: Certainty and feasibility
guide.rule: Keep useful, possible and likely distinct. A viable plan can work in practice; an unattainable goal cannot be reached in the stated circumstances.
guide.example: The plan aims to reduce the amount of waste.

guide.title: Forms and resource use
guide.rule: Efficient means avoiding waste; effective means achieving the intended result. Renewable, recyclable and rechargeable describe different properties.
guide.example: The machine uses energy more efficiently.

guide.title: Work vocabulary
guide.rule: Distinguish employee from employer, economic from economical, and salary from hourly or weekly wages. Staff is collective; use a member of staff for one person.
guide.example: The company employs staff on different shifts.

guide.title: People, acts and responses
guide.rule: Crime names an offence and criminal can name a person or modify a noun. Learn impose a fine, enforce a law and crime prevention as combinations.
guide.example: The programme focuses on crime prevention.

guide.title: Reporting and judgement
guide.rule: A source may contain facts, interpretations and opinions. Verification checks details; sensationalist writing emphasises dramatic impact.
guide.example: The journalist checked the details before publication.

guide.title: Artistic meanings
guide.rule: Taste can mean personal preference. An electric atmosphere is exciting; a novel approach is new. Choose senses that fit the artistic context.
guide.example: The exhibition includes paintings and wooden carvings.

guide.title: Read the whole entry
guide.rule: Check part of speech, pronunciation, example, register and collocations. A transitive use has an object; the same verb may have an intransitive use elsewhere.
guide.example: The dictionary gives examples of each meaning.

guide.title: Build an active word record
guide.rule: Record forms, spelling, usage and context. Compare analyse / analysis / analytical and learn patterns such as consistent with.
guide.example: The results are consistent with the earlier findings.

guide.title: Describe displayed evidence
guide.rule: Select main features and comparisons. Distinguish rising to a final value from rising by a change, and avoid inventing causes from a chart alone.
guide.example: The number of visitors increased steadily.

guide.title: Link ideas by purpose
guide.rule: Choose links for contrast, result, example or addition. Although introduces a clause; despite commonly introduces a noun phrase or ing form.
guide.example: The conclusion summarises the main argument.

title: General Training Writing
test: Letters, purpose, tone and essay language

guide.title: Purpose and tone
guide.rule: A letter may enquire, apply, apologise, complain or thank. Choose a consistent tone, and use patterns such as sorry for and look forward to hearing.
guide.example: I am writing to enquire about the course.
